stories.headline: ESPN's full, final Phantom Draft for 2026: 63 picks, bids aplenty, live trades
stories.summary: It's finally here. Jasper Chellappah's full, final Phantom Draft for ESPN ahead of the 2026 AFL Draft. 63 picks, bids at the top of the order, and live trades.
stories.body:
We're finally here. After 12 months of scrutiny and assessment the 2026 AFL Draft class is ripe for the picking across Thursday and Friday nights.

This is ESPN's full, final Phantom Draft. 63 picks in total, with the first nine club selections remaining the same from the original Phantom Draft five weeks ago.

Dougie Cochrane will be crowned pick 1 and Ethan Drever remains the firm favourite to land at childhood club Essendon. From there conjecture ensues. Arki Butler's links to Richmond have strengthened of late and West Coast is primed to take the best WA prospect available since Luke Jackson in Heath Mellody.

Melbourne's play to move up for the best key defender in the pool remains the likelihood, but the Tigers with pick four is where the draft can turn. Various iterations will be pinned on Richmond's decision with their second pick after paying a considerable price to move up in the trade period.

Within this Phantom Draft there are live trades predicted. GWS is favoured in a race to trade for Port Adelaide's pick 12; expect picks in return of 20, 26 and a future second-rounder. Adelaide has been desperate to move up the board and are predicted to execute a deal for Carlton's pick 13 and 50 in return for 15, 43 and a future second. Port Adelaide moves up for Brisbane's pick 21 with pick 34 and Richmond's future second, and Carlton nabs West Coast's second-rounder with a future first round pick due to the Eagles' list crunch only allowing for three selections at the draft - albeit the Eagles are attempting to consolidate their selections into another first-rounder.

These four potential first-round trades are accounted for in this Phantom Draft.

Recruiters will earn their money this year - the crop is extremely even from 10 through 40 and there's an element of list need that plays into proceedings when the talent available is so close.

Ahead of Thursday's first round, this is ESPN's prediction of all 63 picks in the 2026 AFL Draft.

Previous Power Rankings: April | May | June | July | August | September | October | November

Other stuff to know: Draft primer and FAQs | Every club's needs | Draft order | Jasper's first Phantom Draft | Full combine wrap and results

1. BID: Port Adelaide - Dougie Cochrane

Port Adelaide, FWD/DEF, 196cm

The consensus best prospect in the draft. Cochrane is commanding in the air as a key forward, has the athleticism and ball use to intercept and damage from the backline and boasts aspirations to play through the midfield. He will be the first prospect in years to be drafted at pick one without playing a single U18s national championships game, such is his talent. Port Adelaide has no issues going into future deficit to match this bid.

READ: Consensus top AFL draft prospect Dougie Cochrane already in rare air

2. Essendon - Ethan Drever

GWV Rebels, MID, 188cm

Drever has been the slight favourite for the open pool no. 1 slot since the trade period and nothing has changed. He's a dynamic midfielder with the explosive traits that befit the modern game. The Dons are keen but won't anoint their pick until the night.

In the mix: Arki Butler

READ: Power to burn and a 'trademark' goal: why Drever rocketed up draft boards

3. BID: Carlton - Cody Walker

Carlton VFL, MID, 184cm

Carlton supporters have been eagerly awaiting the arrival of Walker. A ball magnet through the midfield with a beautiful blend of inside-outside ball-winning, Walker is balanced, agile and determined to be the best footballer he can be. Richmond has had a good look at him through their NGA as an indigenous prospect but he's chosen his father Andrew's path with the Blues. Carlton will match with a deficit on their future first-rounder.

READ: 'I'm a competitor': Cody Walker primed and ready for the next step

4. Richmond - Arki Butler

Sandringham Dragons, FWD, 184cm

Clubs are aware of Richmond's interest in Butler, possibly the most unique top draft prospect in recent years. He's all damage, racking up goals and goal assists in the forward half with the best one-on-one work for his size since Toby Greene.

In the mix: Ethan Drever, Heath Mellody

READ: 'All damage' - Arki Butler is the 2026 draft's most watchable junior footballer

5. West Coast - Heath Mellody

Claremont, MID, 183cm

Mellody is WA's best prospect since Luke Jackson. A smooth-moving midfielder, he's the Larke Medallist and produced a stellar finish to the season in Claremont's WAFL side on the way to a grand final appearance. Mellody runs hard and racks up the ball to hurt opposition with his disposal.

In the mix: Arki Butler, Ethan Drever

READ: Relative obscurity to pick 1 buzz: WA's Heath Mellody is the ultimate bolter

6. BID: GWS - Ethan Matthews

Giants Academy, MID, 185cm

Matthews would have a lot more fanfare if he was in the open draft. His first game for the Allies was some of the best football produced all season through the midfield, and he reminds some recruiters of a young Scott Pendlebury with his composure as a tall left footer. Richmond could bid on Matthews before this point but don't expect him to slide past Sydney - GWS will match wherever the bid lies as the top Giants Academy prospect since Tom Green.

7. Melbourne - Mitch Harris

Woodville-West Torrens, DEF, 196cm

The best key defender in the draft has been mocked by ESPN to Melbourne since the trade period ended. Harris intercepts with the best and can lock down on genuine key forwards at his 196cm. He's competitive, composed and athletic with natural defensive instincts. The Dees traded up with Port Adelaide for this selection to effectively bypass North Melbourne who had eyes set on Harris before the Nick Blakey trade.

In the mix: Arki Butler, Gus Teixeira

READ: Key defender Mitch Harris bolting up AFL Draft boards at the eleventh hour

8. Richmond - Harry Van Hattum

Northern Knights, RUC, 205cm

The remainder of the first round hinges on this decision. The Tigers have kept cards close to their chest, just like last year when they opted for Sam Grlj against industry expectations. Trading up for this pick means they have had a prospect in mind and Van Hattum projects as the natural heir for Toby Nankervis. He's physical and gifted in the ruck, plus has the skill and athletic profile to be that next generation of ruck that impacts games.

In the mix: Gus Teixeira, Mitch Harris

READ: 'I just hate that': Harry Van Hattum wants to end ruck disrespect

9. Sydney - Gustavo Teixeira

Sandringham Dragons, MID/FWD, 182cm

A powerful forward-half midfielder, Teixeira exploded onto the scene early this year but has battled through illness and injury. It makes it all the more impressive how good his national carnival was, and the Swans have long been linked since trading into this selection. If Richmond opts for Teixeira they may look to a key position option.

In the mix: Clancy Snell, Sam Gayfer

READ: Despite injury and illness, Gustavo Teixeira is still one of this year's top prospects

10. Gold Coast - Tyson Bradley

Sandringham Dragons, DEF, 196cm

The Suns are planning for life after the 32-year-old Sam Collins who has been an underrated star for a long time. Bradley has a mature body and sets himself to take on and beat the best key forward of the opposition, winning Vic Metro's MVP in a stellar carnival.

In the mix: Leo Steed, Clancy Snell

11. St Kilda - Sam Gayfer

Northern Knights, FWD, 194cm

The best performed key forward this year is in high demand. Gayfer can leap on heads and thrives on the lead where he creates separation and protects the ball. He's a competitor that could play at either end of the ground for the Saints, though a key defender here also suits depending on how the board plays out.

In the mix: Tyson Bradley, Clancy Snell

12. Collingwood - Clancy Snell

Gippsland Power, DEF, 197cm

The Pies got a good look at Snell at VFL level. He's an aggressive interceptor that also won his one-on-ones at Talent League level. His best traits come in the air with strong hands and beautiful reading of the play behind the ball. If Gayfer is available he's the obvious pick, but Collingwood may struggle to trade up the order with future selections worth less in the Tasmania era. If Richmond opts against Van Hattum he could slide through a host of teams willing to bypass a ruck and land here.

In the mix: Sam Gayfer, Tyson Bradley

13. Adelaide - Lochie Burrows

Sandringham Dragons, MID/DEF, 182cm

The Crows trade up two spots for the opportunity to land more midfield talent. Burrows has the versatility to impact across the ground and brings best 23 depth immediately with the upside to be an excellent defensive midfielder. His suitors are numbered in the teens as one of the best characters in this draft class.

In the mix: Leo Steed, Clancy Snell

14. BID: Brisbane - Caylen Murray

Lions Academy, DEF/MID, 184cm

Murray is the next in a long line of Lions Academy stars. The composed halfback uses the ball beautifully and has demonstrated the midfield craft to warrant projections in the engine room soon. Brisbane could forgo matching this bid if it comes in the top 10 but that remains unlikely.

15. Melbourne - Leo Steed

Swan Districts, MID, 177cm

The Dees would be excited to see a mix of midfielders available here if they opt for Harris first up. Steed offers the hard-nosed ball-winning needed for the future and combines it with hard running both ways and good ball use. He's mixed it with senior bodies already in the WAFL and has clubs keen earlier than this point.

In the mix: Toby Krasna, Lochie Burrows

16. GWS - George Dimer

Sandringham Dragons, FWD, 173cm

The residual pick of a move up the draft and matched bid for Matthews lands GWS the genius of the draft class. Dimer is aiming for a 99.95 ATAR and is tossing up between medicine and law at university, all the while being the cleanest player in the draft as a small forward. He offers dash and class in the forward half and is a high character selection in the mould of a Giants forward.

In the mix: Leo Steed, Lochie Burrows

17. St Kilda - Toby Krasna

Northern Knights, MID, 184cm

Krasna is a natural footballer with running power, class by foot and the endeavour to weave his way out of trouble. He looks suited to outside roles where his flair shines through and the Saints are on the lookout for runners to fit around Wanganeen-Milera. A key defender suits if available at this spot and the midfielder may depend on what slides through.

In the mix: Clancy Snell, Lochie Burrows

18. Essendon - Wil Malady

Gippsland Power, FWD, 190cm

Malady is a candidate to slide on draft night as a forward that doesn't quite fit in as a key target at 190cm. He produced two remarkable grand finals performances for Caulfield Grammar and with the Gippsland Power, and has the ability to play up the ground with athleticism or deep in attack as a marking option. Essendon can prioritise who they don't believe gets through to their swathe of second round picks here.

In the mix: George Dimer, Toby Krasna

19. Fremantle - Jake Eime

Central District, DEF, 182cm

The links to Eime at this spot are real, and the only club separating Fremantle from their man is Adelaide before them. The dashing halfback has dare in abundance, tucking the ball under his arm to break lines. He would form a potent combination with Jordan Clark off halfback.

In the mix: Clancy Snell, Jake Soutar

20. Port Adelaide - George Gale

Claremont, MID, 190cm

Port trades up to this selection via Brisbane in this Phantom Draft, and Gale suits as a big-bodied midfielder that can play peripheral roles before moving inside. He played in a WAFL grand final with Claremont and was a strong contributor for WA in the championships with a big engine to get up and down the ground.

In the mix: Kodah Edwards, Wil Malady

21. Essendon - Harvie Cooke

Northern Knights, MID/FWD, 177cm

Cooke has been a star all season, winning the Morrish Medal in the Talent League and proving his worth as a half forward for Vic Metro. His clean hands and versatility appeal for a lot of clubs in this region of the draft.

In the mix: George Dimer, Archie Elliott

22. Port Adelaide - Jackson Phillips

Dandenong Stingrays, MID, 182cm

Phillips has a high floor. He's a strong runner and good ball user on both sides of his body, with the discipline to play as an outside midfielder. There aren't too many midfield prospects in this range of the draft and the Power are keen to address their depth.

In the mix: Jack Pickett, Kodah Edwards

23. Richmond - Noah Williams

Geelong Falcons, MID/DEF, 176cm

Williams has previously been a top five talent for ESPN given his form and class early in the season. Since then he's battled through injury and inconsistency but clubs know his value as an inside midfielder and damaging halfback. That flexibility gives him a safe floor at the next level.

In the mix: Jackson Phillips, Harvie Cooke

24. Carlton - Harvey Spawton-Guy

West Perth, FWD, 196cm

The Blues trade into this pick via the Eagles in this Phantom Draft. The aptly named Spawton-Guy is an elite competitor that can play at either end of the ground and do a job. He makes good on his chances and has the raw attributes to excel in a professional environment.

In the mix: Jack Pickett, Ethan Herbert

25. West Coast - Archie Elliott

GWV Rebels, FWD, 182cm

What a rise this would be for Elliott. Thrown forward this year, he's blossomed as a marking target with a strong goal sense. He positions himself well, protects the ball drop and looks like a natural forward that can play tall and small.

In the mix: Noah Williams, Khaled El Souki

26. Port Adelaide - Archie Van Dyk

South Adelaide, MID, 191cm

Van Dyk has been out of sight, out of mind for a large part of the year, but his elite ball-winning and size around the contest is appealing for clubs. He's courageous and presents as a fantastic character addition to squads after prevailing through difficult circumstances this year to play fantastic football in the SANFL Reserves.

In the mix: Kodah Edwards, Khaled El Souki

27. Essendon - Jack Pickett

Geelong Falcons, FWD, 194cm

Pickett tore his ACL and MCL early this season, but was a genuine top 10 contender before his horrible injury. He has natural forward craft in his leading patterns plus offers strong hands in the air and one of the best set shot routines to come through elite pathways in some time.

In the mix: Harvey Spawton-Guy, Kodah Edwards

28. Brisbane - Kodah Edwards

South Adelaide, MID/FWD, 183cm

Edwards would be a candidate to slide further if not for the flashes of genuine upside as a forward 50 target. He's a natural ball-winner through the midfield and enjoyed a stellar carnival but his competitiveness, defensive endeavour and goalkicking penchant in the forward half gives him versatility to play a number of roles.

In the mix: Koby LeCras, George Gale

29. Hawthorn - Harrison Chapman

Eastern Ranges, MID, 190cm

The upside is there to see for Chapman. He's a smooth-moving outside midfielder that thrives in transition with a good athletic foundation and tidy skills. He has ambitions to become an on-baller which would make this a smash pick if it eventuates.

In the mix: Marlon Neocleous, Lachie Hicks

30. Collingwood - Gus Kennedy

Dandenong Stingrays, DEF/MID, 188cm

Long linked to the Pies, Kennedy is tough and aggressive in his play off halfback and has the traits to move into the midfield down the line. He's a high character prospect that can play in a variety of roles and suits the Pies's vision for readymade prospects.

In the mix: Albert MacGowan, Archie Van Dyk

31. Carlton - Marlon Neocleous

Gippsland Power, FWD, 167cm

An energetic small forward who looks most at home when venturing further afield, Neocleous offers tricks and class with ball in hand. He executes well under pressure and bites off aggressive kicks to link the play despite his size.

In the mix: Ethan Herbert, Koby LeCras

32. BID: Western Bulldogs - Khaled El Souki

Western Jets, FWD, 176cm

Any earlier and there's a chance this bid doesn't get matched by the Dogs. El Souki is a natural forward-half player with the strength to play through contact and a beautiful left foot kick around goals. He matched it in his sole VFL appearance for Footscray after dominating the Talent League.

33. BID: Hawthorn - Keenan Boi

Gippsland Power, FWD, 177cm

Boi will be an excellent role player at the next level. As a forward he straight lines the ball with strength through the hips and makes good decisions under pressure. A Hawks NGA prospect, he has interest earlier than this point which would make matching a bid before Hawthorn's first pick a toss up, but they're well suited to claim the forward at this stage of the draft.

34. Adelaide - Albert MacGowan

Sandringham Dragons, MID, 187cm

MacGowan has flown under the radar as a midfielder with a clear role at the next level. He marks the ball superbly at his size around the ground and took out the AFL Draft 2km time trial to showcase his ability to cover the ground off a wing.

In the mix: Billy Wigmore, Wil Antrobus

35. BID: Sydney - Mason McGroder

Swans Academy, DEF, 195cm

McGroder has been one of the stories of the season as an international long jumper that claimed silver at the U20s in Oregon earlier this year. He's chosen a football career as a Swans Academy member and provides an elite athletic profile at a potential key position size to develop.

36. North Melbourne - Billy Wigmore

Western Jets, DEF, 188cm

Wigmore is one of the best interceptors in the class with his reading of the play and strong hands. The rest of his game needs to be rounded out but it's a transferable skill that suits North's list build.

In the mix: Marlon Neocleous, Darcy Szerszyn

37. Brisbane - Koby LeCras

West Perth, FWD, 192cm

LeCras would be a slider here based on talent. He's an exceptional mover at 192cm that impacts aerially and offers an assured left foot kick in front of goals. He partially tore his ACL in his WAFL debut this year but returned to run the 2km at the AFL Draft combine.

In the mix: Billy Wigmore, Darcy Szerszyn

READ: From an ACL tear to a time trial PB: Koby LeCras on building resilience in his draft year

38. Adelaide - Gabe Patterson

Glenelg, FWD, 184cm

Patterson is an aggressive small forward with some big game performances to back his credentials. The SA product straight lines the ball and has the power to mix it with senior bodies early on.

In the mix: Ethan Herbert, Wil Antrobus

39. Geelong - Lachie Hicks

Western Jets, MID, 184cm

Hicks has the athletic profile and thirst to be an AFL midfielder that suits Geelong down to the ground. His ball use needs work but the rest of his game as a midfielder or half forward is exciting, with the ability to rack up the footy and impact in the forward half.

In the mix: Billy Wigmore, Zach Stevens

40. Fremantle - Jake Soutar

East Perth, DEF, 190cm

What a result for the Dockers if local product Jake Soutar makes it through to this selection. The readymade defender took out East Perth's fairest and best as a 20-year-old and has incredible sense in the air of when to intercept and when to spoil. He looks most suited as a third tall at the next level.

In the mix: Brady Wright, Jack Slattery

41. St Kilda - Darcy Szerszyn

Dandenong Stingrays, DEF, 188cm

There are a few general defenders in this range of the draft and Szerszyn is perhaps the most interesting prospect given his athletic profile and flashes of attacking vigour off halfback. He can play on talls and smalls, has the ball use to reliably kick in from defence and offers big upside in a professional environment.

In the mix: Jacob McNicol, Jackson Watkins

42. Carlton - Ethan Herbert

North Adelaide, RUC, 200cm

Herbert may slide on draft night as the second ruckman in this draft. He's the type of extra midfielder that clubs covet when the ball hits the ground, linking play by hands and getting around the ground with a strong endurance base. He will need to add size and hopefully grow to a genuine ruck size in time.

In the mix: Benji Van Rooyen, Xavier Ladbrook

43. Richmond - Wil Antrobus

Dandenong Stingrays, DEF, 182cm

Antrobus makes up for his lack of size with an impressive attack on the footy, but his clear best trait is the beautiful left foot kick out of defence. He's a reliable kick in option that generates penetration and can pinpoint targets with a lovely action.

In the mix: Sam Devers, Darcy Szerszyn

44. BID: Essendon - Blake Justice

Calder Cannons, MID, 192cm

Essendon will be delighted if a bid on their NGA extends past their glut of second round picks. The dynamic midfielder has a unique blend of size at 192cm and speed at 2.8 seconds in the 20m sprint. He will rehab a hamstring injury suffered at the state combine early in the pre-season.

45. Sydney - Jack Slattery

Woodville-West Torrens, FWD, 192cm

Slattery starred at the national championships as an over-ager and his accurate set shot routine plus capacity to create separation on the lead are transferable to the next level. Despite being undersized he has the AFL attributes to perform at the next level.

In the mix: Brady Wright, Sam Devers

46. Brisbane - Jordan Knapp

Eastern Ranges, MID, 180cm

Knapp is a genuine ball magnet, working hard to get to contests and outnumber. He's slight of size and lacks penetration in his kick but is clean and incisive with his hands as a midfielder to develop.

In the mix: Xavier Ladbrook, Memphis Webb

47. Port Adelaide - Xavier Ladbrook

Gippsland Power, DEF, 203cm

Port could draft what is potentially the fourth-best key defender in the pool. Ladbrook will take time to develop given his slim frame but is an excellent runner and reliable ball user out of the back half, and the Power can afford to wait on his talents.

In the mix: Jack Watkins, Sam Devers

48. BID: Fremantle - Finlay Yeo

East Fremantle, FWD, 172cm

Yeo is diminutive but uses it to his advantage, weaving through traffic and creating havoc both with the ball and as a defensive forward. Linked to Fremantle through their NGA, the small forward has offered exciting glimpses as a clean midfielder that can spit forward to impact.

49. Sydney - Andrio Sousa

Dandenong Stingrays, FWD/MID, 182cm

Sousa blitzed the combine and that power comes through in the tape. As a half forward he can push up to stoppages and burst away from opponents with speed to impact ahead of the ball, but could also play as a winger with good aerobic capacity.

In the mix: Cody Templeton, Sam Devers

50. Melbourne - Brady Wright

Werribee VFL, FWD, 195cm

A mature-age key forward, Wright's stellar season for Werribee culminated in the Fothergill-Round-Mitchell Medal as the best young player in the VFL. He's excellent on the move on the forward 50 and has a repeatable set shot. Wright will play significant senior football at the next level.

In the mix: Sam Devers, Jack Slattery

51. North Melbourne - Sam Devers

Eastern Ranges, DEF, 189cm

Devers has the athletic profile and size clubs covet late in the draft, with significant upside to eventually contribute at AFL level. He breaks lines with power and can lace out targets as he gets up the ground, though it may take time to round out his defensive game.

In the mix: Kale Matthews-Hampton, Jacob McNicol

52. Melbourne - Benji Van Rooyen

Claremont, RUC, 203cm

It would be fitting for the Dees to take a swing on their ruck of the future here if Van Hattum is bypassed early. Van Rooyen has the familial connection with brother Jacob, but was also the best-performed ruck at the national championships with strong craft in the air and unselfish body work around the ball. He would take time to develop under Max Gawn.

In the mix: Ethan Herbert, Jack Watkins

53. Geelong - Zach Stevens

Geelong VFL, FWD, 183cm

Stevens is a 19-year-old that impressed after being elevated to Geelong's VFL side as a half forward. He plays with speed and urgency with the ball in hand, creating opportunities through separation and natural smarts around goal.

In the mix: Kale Matthews-Hampton, Sam Devers

54. West Coast - Harper Banfield

Claremont, MID/FWD, 181cm

The Eagles would prefer to get up the order to nab another first round pick with their second-rounders but are hamstrung by their compensation pick only being made available on night two. As it stands they're keen to get Banfield into the club after missing out on his brother last year, with Harper offering elite endurance around the ground with a mature body to play inside and out.

55. GWS - Judd Burgiel

Gippsland Power, DEF, 179cm

Burgiel plays at a frenetic pace that can be hard to contain. He's explosive and loves to tuck the ball and run to break lines, plus has a hard edge that lends itself to locking down on opponents.

In the mix: Cody Templeton, Benji Van Rooyen

56. Geelong - Zac Antonellos

Eastern Ranges, FWD, 181cm

Antonellos makes his opportunities count as a small forward. He's extremely clean and crumbs packs adeptly around goal, giving himself every opportunity to create shots on goal or set teammates up under pressure.

In the mix: Sam Tassone, Charlie Gray

57. North Melbourne - Aidan McCartney

Swans Academy, FWD, 195cm

McCartney missed the full season with a hip injury, but was highly rated as an undersized key position player entering 2026. North is keen to add him to their main list as a father-son prospect that could develop at either end of the ground.

58. Collingwood - Harry Franz

Glenelg, DEF, 193cm

Franz has some very exciting traits as an aerialist in the defensive 50. He leaps on heads and plays with an edge that befits key backs at the next level whether it be intercepting or locking down. There's scope for him to play at either end of the ground.

59. Collingwood - Kai Parker

Northern Knights, DEF, 189cm

Parker has trained with the Pies over pre-season but missed a chunk of the year with a shoulder concern and glandular fever. At his best his athleticism matches the trends of modern footy and he looks suited to roles up the ground.

In the mix: Benji Van Rooyen, Jackson Watkins

60. Hawthorn - Cooper Hodge

Lions Academy, MID/DEF, 183cm

The son of Hawks legend Luke Hodge, there are some similarities in the game of Cooper. He's a natural defensive presence with discipline and toughness but has shown most of his traits through the midfield to date with clean ball-winning and tackling pressure at the coalface.

61. Western Bulldogs - Tate Hodgson

Northern Knights, DEF, 197cm

Hodgson was a stalwart for the Knights this year and only slides due to concerns around his athleticism at the next level. He's a natural key defender at 197cm and consistently gets himself into the right positions to bring the ball to ground.

In the mix: Marcus Prasad, Kale Matthews-Hampton

62. Port Adelaide - Jackson Watkins

Calder Cannons, FWD, 185cm

Port's sixth and final pick would be a steal if Watkins gets this far in the draft. At 185cm he has real burst from stoppage, but likely settles into the forward 50 with his work off the ball to pressure, harass and play through contact.

In the mix: Memphis Webb, Ethan Herbert

63. Western Bulldogs - Memphis Webb

North Adelaide, MID, 184cm

Webb is a midfielder with the defensive traits to unlock the offensive threats of those around him. He plays with physicality at a mature size despite only being 183cm and his tackling is a feature of his game at stoppages.

In the mix: Marcus Prasad, Kale Matthews-Hampton

stories.headline: Sources: MLS side FC Cincy nearing deal to acquire NWSL's Racing
stories.summary: The ownership groups of MLS side FC Cincinnati and the NWSL's Racing Louisville FC are nearing an agreement that would relocate the NWSL team to Cincinnati in 2028, multiple sources told ESPN.
stories.body:
The ownership groups of MLS side FC Cincinnati and the NWSL's Racing Louisville FC are nearing an agreement that would relocate the NWSL team to Cincinnati in 2028, multiple sources told ESPN.

Racing Louisville said in a statement on Tuesday that the team is "actively working through a process to sell" the team, although it did not name a prospective buyer. No agreement has been finalized yet, sources said, and it is not immediately clear what a final sale price could be for the NWSL team.

If a deal is reached, Racing Louisville would play the 2027 NWSL season at Lynn Family Stadium in Louisville, Kentucky, before operations moved 100 miles northeast to Cincinnati in 2028. Once there, Racing would play at TQL Stadium, the 26,000-seat downtown home of the MLS side.

ESPN first reported in September that the two sides were engaged in negotiations.

Soccer Holdings and chairman John Neace own Racing Louisville and began seeking investment earlier this year, as ESPN reported in May.

"As the NWSL has grown, so have the financial demands of competing in the league. Additional investment is needed to support the club's long-term future, and we are actively working through a process to sell Racing to a new ownership group," the Louisville-based club said in a statement Tuesday. "Racing was established to bring top-tier women's professional sports to Louisville -- something meaningful our community could rally around. That vision became reality because of the fans, partners and community members who believed in it and continue to support the club. We are deeply grateful for their roles in making Racing what it is today.

"Further updates will be shared as appropriate. In the meantime, our focus is on supporting our players and staff ahead of the 2027 season."

FC Cincinnati also inquired about purchasing Racing Louisville in recent years, ESPN previously reported. On each previous occasion, however, sources cited personal relationships between ownership groups as an obstacle to a potential sale.

An FC Cincinnati spokesperson provided the following statement to ESPN on Tuesday: "We understand and appreciate the excitement and interest around the possibility of bringing an NWSL team to Cincinnati. The passion for soccer in this community is undeniable, and FC Cincinnati remains deeply committed to supporting the continued growth of the women's game. We are hard at work exploring opportunities to expand our involvement in women's soccer, and we are hopeful to have an update in the near future."

Recently, the situation in Louisville has become more urgent. Racing joined the NWSL ahead of the 2021 NWSL season for an expansion fee of around $2 million. Investment in the league by new owners of other clubs has increased exponentially since then. Expansion teams in Atlanta and Columbus will begin playing in the NWSL in 2028 after paying $165 million and $205 million fees, respectively.

Sources told ESPN that throughout the year NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman has been heavily involved in the process of finding a solution in Louisville.

"Their ownership group has made clear that they are prepared to sell," NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman told ESPN in August. "The trajectory of this league has an investment thesis. Our owners, and the future of the league, need to be aligned in that investment thesis.

"They [Louisville] have made clear that they're not prepared to sign up for that. And so, they're raising capital because they want more financial support to be able to invest in the team, which is an indication of their understanding of what's required."

Racing Louisville averaged just under 5,500 fans per game this year, down slightly from 2025. Only the Chicago Stars averaged fewer fans per game.

Sources across the league said to ESPN that Columbus' $205 million price tag paid earlier this year ostensibly sets a floor for any future team, while adding that the NWSL is exercising caution about any potential sale price for a relocation of Racing Louisville to Cincinnati since those cities are only about 100 miles apart.

FC Cincinnati unsuccessfully bid for a 2026 NWSL expansion team with a group that, at the time, included WNBA star Caitlin Clark. Denver was ultimately awarded that team, the NWSL's 14th, for $110 million.

Racing Louisville was recently valued at $127 million and $140 million by Sportico and Forbes, respectively, ranking it as one of the least valuable franchises in the NWSL.

"Relocation should be a last resort," Berman said in March about her philosophy at large. "We view, in our philosophy of what our teams are, is driven by the idea that these are community assets. And what that means is that the community has to believe and it has to be demonstrated over time, that owners and the league will keep these teams in markets even through periods of transition, team sales, or other ups and downs that might be happening with the club, with their on-field performance.

"That does not mean that it's a red line. It means that we will only consider that under appropriate circumstances, and we will be very judicious and exercise high discretion in those circumstances where we feel that it's appropriate."

Versions of relocation have happened in the past in the NWSL. The North Carolina Courage were previously the Western New York Flash until moving in January of 2017. The NWSL also had a franchise leave Kansas City for Salt Lake City, Utah, then return to Kansas City. Both markets now have teams after the Utah Royals were revived in 2024.

stories.headline: Toronto Tempo win 2027 WNBA draft lottery, land No. 1 pick
stories.summary: The Tempo won the WNBA draft lottery Sunday night, earning the No. 1 pick and potentially the chance to draft USC star JuJu Watkins. The Comets will choose second, followed by the Mystics.
stories.body:
The Toronto Tempo will have the No. 1 pick in the 2027 WNBA draft after winning the draft lottery Sunday night.

After completing its inaugural season in 2026, Toronto becomes the first franchise to have the top pick heading into its second season since the Dream in 2009, when Atlanta selected Angel McCoughtry. The Tempo will make their selection April 12.

Lottery odds are based on teams' two-year cumulative records, except for Portland and Toronto, which were expansion teams in 2026. Their odds were solely based on their records from this past season.

The Houston Comets, formerly the Connecticut Sun (22-66), and Toronto (11-33) had the best odds to land the No. 1 pick, each with 329 chances out of 1,000. This marked the first time since 2015 that two teams had the same odds for the first selection.

The Sun, relocating to Texas from Connecticut this offseason, went 1-2 against Toronto in 2026 -- which is the first tiebreaker -- so the franchise couldn't fall past the third pick. Toronto was guaranteed at least the fourth selection.

"I [felt] like something amazing was going to happen," said Tempo forward Aneesah Morrow, the team's lottery representative. "We're here now ... The future is bright. We have great and amazing players, and we have a country on our back. It feels different when you play like that."

Houston will select second in the draft. All of the other selections are in line with what the odds projected heading into Sunday. Washington, which had the next-best odds after acquiring Chicago's first-round pick in the trade that sent Ariel Atkins to the Sky, will pick third.

Seattle will select at No. 4, followed by Portland at No. 5. The Los Angeles Sparks have the sixth and seventh picks -- one that is their own and the other acquired from Phoenix in the Kelsey Plum trade in August.

USC's JuJu Watkins is projected to go No. 1 in ESPN's latest mock draft released Thursday, with Texas' Madison Booker slotted at No. 2.

Notre Dame's Hannah Hidalgo, Virginia's Kymora Johnson, LSU's Mikaylah Williams, Kansas' S'Mya Nichols and Sarah Cisse of France are projected to round out the lottery picks.

The Tempo had a strong start to their season before veteran Brittney Sykes was sidelined indefinitely because of a plantar fascia injury. After she went down, Toronto went 4-21, including a 12-game losing streak. But Sykes and Marina Mabrey combined to form one of the highest-scoring backcourts in the league.

Toronto has some young talent in Morrow, whom the team acquired in a midseason trade, and last year's No. 6 pick Kiki Rice, who was the team's third-leading scorer but missed nearly two months because of a Grade 2 left ankle sprain. The combination of Mabrey, Sykes and Rice gives the Tempo perimeter depth. However, they are somewhat thin in the front court.

"[Toronto] is amazing," Morrow said. "Ever since I walked in the locker room, from the beginning, I was able to see the chemistry ... it's all about building the future of the Toronto franchise."

The WNBA schedule will increase from 44 to 50 games in the 2027 season, making it the longest in league history. The added games were part of the new collective bargaining agreement, which also vastly increased pay, secured a $2.2 billion media deal and slated six expansion teams to join the league between 2024 and 2030.

The 2027 WNBA season is expected to start May 7 and has a latest possible end date of Oct. 24, sources told ESPN's Alexa Philippou last week.

"We're excited about the momentum; it's never been stronger," said Bethany Donaphin, senior vice president and head of WNBA league operations. "We think there's a demand, and we're excited to expand to 50 games."

The rest of the first-round draft order is: No. 8 New York, No. 9 Dallas, No. 10 Indiana, No. 11 Chicago, No. 12 Chicago, No. 13 Dallas, No. 14 Golden State and No. 15 Minnesota.

stories.headline: Kangaroos bounce Kiwis for fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup title
stories.summary: The Kangaroos have won a fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup, toppling New Zealand 32-12 in Brisbane.
stories.body:
The Kangaroos have punished a disappointing New Zealand, with Reece Walsh running riot in a 32-12 World Cup final waltz.

There was an expectation the Kiwis, searching for their second Cup title and first since 2008, would push Australia all the way after a two-point loss in a pulsating tournament opener.

But the visitors struggled from the outset in Brisbane on Sunday night, Jamayne Isaako's kick-off floating long in a sign of things to come.

Walsh dazzled at fullback for the Kangaroos, his pace, vision and wicked footwork too much as he helped lay on two tries and generally wreak havoc around the ruck and close to the line.

Conversely, Walsh's New Zealand opposite Kalyn Ponga -- International Rugby League's Golden Boot winner on Thursday night -- was unable to get into game.

Australian hooker Harry Grant and halves Tom Dearden and Cam Munster completely outplayed their error-riddled opposites, while the Kangaroos' pack muscled up.

Dearden laid on two first-half tries for Liam Martin with well-timed short balls, while Bradman Best was rewarded for an inspired chase-down tackle of Jahrome Hughes with a try soon after.

When Tom Trbojevic scored to begin the second half it was 28-6 and effectively game over.

Jack Bostock completed his breakout season with a try in each half for Australia.

It was the Kangaroos' fourth consecutive title and 10th in the last 11 tournaments, dating back to 1975.

stories.headline: NBA Power Rankings, Week 4: One wild stat for all 30 teams
stories.summary: Here's where all 30 teams rank this week -- along with one remarkable stat that has fueled each franchise through one month of the season.
stories.body:
The first month of the 2026-2027 NBA season is in the books!

In the surprisingly deep West, the San Antonio Spurs continue to pace the conference, with a point differential of plus-11.2.

The next four teams in the West -- the Minnesota Timberwolves, Memphis Grizzlies, Houston Rockets and Los Angeles Lakers -- would all rank No. 2 in the East.

Speaking of the East, the Boston Celtics continue to surge, outscoring opponents by an average of 11.5 points per game, while the Philadelphia 76ers, despite a 12-3 record, have beat teams by just 2.8 points per game. The Detroit Pistons, last year's No. 1 seed, continue to sputter, while the 2026 champion New York Knicks are 8-6 -- sixth in a wide-open conference.

In this week's Power Rankings, our insiders rank each of the 30 teams and also highlight one illuminating statistic per team to watch over the coming months.

Here's our 1-30 breakdown.

Previous rankings: Oct. 28 | Nov. 4 | Nov. 11

Jump to a team:

ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE

DAL | DEN | DET | GS | HOU | IND

LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN

NO | NY | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX

POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS

1. San Antonio Spurs

2026-27 record: 12-3
Previous ranking: 1
Next games: vs. LAC (Nov. 19), vs. NO (Nov. 21), @ SAC (Nov. 23)

Illuminating number: 12

That's how many wins in a row the Spurs piled up after losing two in a row to start the season.

The last time San Antonio pieced together a 10-game winning streak before the month of December was November 2013, the same season the Spurs captured their fifth NBA championship.

What's more, San Antonio ran off the winning streak playing with an experimental three-guard lineup that the Spurs committed to implementing over the summer. So far, the lineup is working, demonstrating great roster and on-court versatility for San Antonio as its operation evolves around Victor Wembanyama. -- Michael C. Wright

2. Los Angeles Lakers

2026-27 record: 13-2
Previous ranking: 2
Next games: vs. UTAH (Nov. 18), vs. SAC (Nov. 20), vs. UTAH (Nov. 23)

Illuminating number: 504

That's Luka Doncic's point total so far this season, the third most in NBA history through the first 13 games of a season, trailing only Wilt Chamberlain.

Doncic is averaging 39.0 points per game, which would be the third-highest scoring average for a season if he keeps it up, with only Chamberlain ahead of him in the top two spots. -- Dave McMenamin

3. Boston Celtics

2026-27 record: 11-3
Previous ranking: 5
Next games: @ DEN (Nov. 18), @ SAC (Nov. 21), @ GS (Nov. 22), @ WAS (Nov. 24)

Illuminating number: 99.7

Boston is allowing 99.7 points per game on the road, the only team in the league under 100 and almost four points fewer than the next-closest team, the Charlotte Hornets (103.8).

The Celtics were the league's fourth-best defense last season but allowed 107.3 points per game on the road in the regular season, which was still the best in the league. If they hold to this stout defensive start, they'd be the first team to hold road opponents to under 100 points per game since the San Antonio Spurs and Utah Jazz did it in the 2016-17 season. -- Kris Rhim

4. Philadelphia 76ers

2026-27 record: 12-3
Previous ranking: 4
Next games: @ ORL (Nov. 18), vs. MIL (Nov. 21), vs. POR (Nov. 23)

Illuminating number: Plus-2.8

The Sixers have the best record in the Eastern Conference and their second-best start in the past 40 seasons. But they've jumped out to that start without exactly dominating their opponents, with just a 2.8-point average differential, ranking 11th in the NBA.

According to ESPN's BPI, the Sixers have an expected win percentage of 60.1%, which is significantly lower than their actual 80% winning percentage.

Sixers guard VJ Edgecombe acknowledged this point following a win over the Nets:

"We haven't had ... a dominant win yet that we know we're capable of." -- Rhim

5. Houston Rockets

2026-27 record: 11-4
Previous ranking: 7
Next games: @ IND (Nov. 18), @ DEN (Nov. 20), vs. LAC (Nov. 23)

Illuminating number: 9th

That's where the Houston Rockets rank in the NBA in assist-to-turnover ratio after finishing No. 27 last season, which played a major role in the Rockets posting a 22-23 record last season in clutch-time games.

The return of veteran point guard Fred VanVleet is driving Houston's improvement, and the numbers will be even better when the 32-year-old is able to play the second night of back-to-backs as he recovers from last year's ACL surgery. -- Wright

6. Minnesota Timberwolves

2026-27 record: 11-4
Previous ranking: 6
Next games: vs. NYK (Nov. 19), vs. MEM (Nov. 21), vs. BKN (Nov. 23)

Illuminating number: Plus-12.6

No Anthony Edwards? No problem for the Timberwolves (at least not yet). Minnesota has posted a blistering plus-12.6 net rating when LaMelo Ball shares the court with Ayo Dosunmu, Edwards' replacement in the starting lineup.

For comparison's sake, the Spurs hold the NBA's best overall net rating at ... wait for it ... plus-12.6.

Dosunmu has picked a great time to shoot the lights out: The 2021 second-round pick is averaging a career-high 17.8 points per game on 52/43/91 splits.

Timberwolves executive Tim Connelly should be charged with grand larceny for plucking Dosunmu from the Bulls before last season's trade deadline. -- Ben Golliver

7. Portland Trail Blazers

2026-27 record: 9-5
Previous ranking: 11
Next games: @ MIL (Nov. 19), @ NYK (Nov. 21), @ PHI (Nov. 23)

Illuminating number: 32.1%

Opposing teams are shooting just 32.1% on 3-pointers against Portland, the lowest mark in the NBA.

The Blazers, who have made 56 more 3-pointers than they have allowed through 13 games, are outscoring opponents by an average of 12.9 points per game from beyond the arc.

Given that Portland's offense also ranks among the league's best in generating free throw attempts, it's no surprise the Blazers have jumped up to sixth in offense after finishing 21st last season. -- Golliver

8. Detroit Pistons

2026-27 record: 9-4
Previous ranking: 8
Next games: @ NO (Nov. 18), vs. TOR (Nov. 20), @ ATL (Nov. 22), @ ORL (Nov. 24)

Illuminating number: 8.6

Rebounds averaged by small forward Ausar Thompson. The fourth-year vet has been asked to contribute more on the glass and as a playmaker, but because of the absence of center Jalen Duren, Thompson's dramatic increase on the boards has been critical in keeping the Pistons afloat.

The 6-foot-7 Thompson ranks 18th in the league in rebounding. Grizzlies wing Cedric Coward is the only other swingman who ranks in the top 55.

Thompson has become more of an offensive initiator, too, as J.B. Bickerstaff works to lessen the load of Cade Cunningham. While it has been a work in progress, sometimes stifling Thompson's athleticism, he is still averaging more than five assists per game to start the season.

And with the recent injury to Duncan Robinson, Thompson will add even more responsibility on offense to keep Detroit within striking distance in the East. -- Vince Goodwill

9. Oklahoma City Thunder

2026-27 record: 9-5
Previous ranking: 3
Next games: vs. ATL (Nov. 18), vs. NO (Nov. 20), @ MIA (Nov. 22), @ IND (Nov. 23)

Illuminating number: 100

Oklahoma City's offense produces 118.0 points per 100 possessions with back-to-back MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander on the floor -- and only 100.0 when he sits.

It stands to reason that the offense won't be as efficient without one of the league's elite scorers, but the drop-off is much more significant than it has been in the past few seasons.

The hope is that Ajay Mitchell will continue to improve as he gets more reps as the primary initiator in non-SGA lineups. -- Tim MacMahon

10. Denver Nuggets

2026-27 record: 7-5
Previous ranking: 12
Next games: vs. BOS (Nov. 18), vs. HOU (Nov. 20), @ CHI (Nov. 22), vs. DAL (Nov. 24)

Illuminating number: 47.1%

Jamal Murray has made 41 of his 87 attempted 3s through 12 games. Among players who have attempted at least 50 3s, that 47.1% accuracy rate is the best in the NBA.

Murray has been scorching hot. He's shooting 51% overall from the field and 86% from the line, averaging a career-high 26.1 points.

Nuggets coach David Adelman said recently that he believes Murray is performing like one of the best players in the world and it would be discussed more if Denver had won a few more games.

The Nuggets are a reasonable but unspectacular 7-5, thriving with Murray on the floor (plus-59) but drowning when he sits (minus-51). -- Anthony Slater

11. Memphis Grizzlies

2026-27 record: 10-4
Previous ranking: 13
Next games: @ CLE (Nov. 18), vs. GS (Nov. 19), @ MIN (Nov. 21), @ CHA (Nov. 23)

Illuminating number: 7-0

That's Memphis' road record this season. The Grizzlies have won seven in a row on the road, which ties a franchise record for the most consecutive road wins at any point of a season (they won seven straight in 2010).

Memphis has a chance to break the record Wednesday at Cleveland. Ty Jerome leads the way for the Grizzlies, averaging a career-high 25.4 points, and he is flanked by a pair of young players on the rise in Cameron Boozer and Cedric Coward.

Boozer ranks as the third player since the merger to rack up at least 200 points, 100 rebounds and 75 assists through 14 career games, joining Ben Simmons (2017-18) and Magic Johnson (1979-80). -- Wright

12. New York Knicks

2026-27 record: 8-6
Previous ranking: 10
Next games: @ MIN (Nov. 19), vs. POR (Nov. 21), vs. IND (Nov. 22)

Illuminating number: 30.4

That's the combined 3-point shooting percentage for OG Anunoby, Mikal Bridges and Josh Hart, a big part of why the Knicks have a 15th-ranked offense. Last year, the Knicks used Mike Brown's "let it fly" ethos to rise to the top three in that category before their improbable playoff run.

stories.headline: How fallen giants and their fans bounce back from scandal, relegation
stories.summary: Some of Europe's greatest teams have suffered relegation as punishment. What might lie ahead for Man City? Past scandals provide a few potential answers.
stories.body:
What does it feel like to realize the club you love is stuck in a doom spiral of its own making?

Whether due to cheating, financial mismanagement or general ineptitude, some of Europe's greatest teams have suffered the ignominy of relegation by means of punishment -- and their supporters have watched it unfold. From Juventus and Fiorentina in Italy to Rangers in Scotland, fans have seen offices stripped bare and managers and players scrambling for places on the first boats off the sinking ship.

But a crisis offers the chance for heroes to drag their team out of the deep while suits swap seats in the boardrooms. And amid schadenfreude, anger and denial, supporters of flawed giants find united through their morbid, self-deprecating humor and fortitude in their situation.

As Manchester City's fans await the results of their appeal and the level of punishment for their 114 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules, they might find some small comfort in seeing how others have bounced back from the depths of despair ... or renewed dread at the tribulations that could lie ahead.

Fleeing for greener pastures

By the time manager Fabio Capello had sprinted to Real Madrid in 2006, taking stars Emerson and Fabio Cannavaro with him, Juventus' offices had already been ransacked.

The "Calciopoli" scandal started as a doping investigation into Juventus, but instead found evidence of attempted match-fixing by executives who manipulated referees and their bosses -- a scandal that also implicated Fiorentina, AC Milan, Reggina and Lazio. Papers, contracts and hard drives were seized by the Guardia di Finanza (Financial Police) on May 18, 2006.

The original swath of punishments was handed out just six days after Italy won the 2006 World Cup. Juventus were hammered the hardest; they were kicked down to Serie B and stripped of their 2005 and 2006 league titles, triggering a flurry of expedited exit strategies.

"This world had been turned upside down," Ibrahimovic wrote in his 2011 autobiography. "It wasn't possible to take it all in. We'd won two titles in a row -- were we going to lose everything? One after one the players got away ... every one of us who were left called our agents: 'Sell us, sell us.'

"Uncertainty and desperation hung in the air ... No way was I going to sacrifice a year in the second division. My best years were in danger of being wasted; I told [agent Mino Raiola], 'Do whatever it takes, just get me out of here.'"

Ibrahimovic watched teammates Lilian Thuram and Gianluca Zambrotta join Barcelona, while Patrick Vieira headed to Internazionale. Didier Deschamps took charge, though he couldn't persuade Ibrahimovic to stay. Ibrahimovic said he'd train but wouldn't play in matches, leading to the striker refusing to get on the bus for a preseason game -- instead, he hid in his room and played video games, eventually joining Vieira at Inter.

"In the years following the scandal, any player who had left Juventus and came back to play would get booed. The fans felt betrayed," Lorenzo Bettoni, Football Italia editor, told ESPN. "Even today, if they come back to the Allianz Stadium, they'll still get booed."

Gianluigi Buffon, Alessandro del Piero, Pavel Nedved and David Trézéguet remained and guided Juventus through Serie B. "We chose to stay together to honour a shirt, a club, a fanbase," Buffon wrote in a column for La Stampa in 2017. "We lost everything to gain things which aren't measurable and can't be bartered: respect, affection."

AC Milan's players feared relegation, too. "The whole thing was an absolute shambles," Andrea Pirlo wrote in "I Think Therefore I Play." "One thing I was sure of, though: I would never drop down to Serie B. And if I had to leave, I wouldn't feel like a traitor. You always want to be ambitious and play for a noble cause. There was no way I was going to pay for other people's sins, if that's what they turned out to be." Ultimately, Milan received a hefty points deduction but remained in Serie A.

Choosing to stay

While some players seek the nearest exit option, others choose to stay. Their club's careworn fans hold them close as symbols of hope and rare loyalty.

When Fiorentina were declared bankrupt due to unpaid debts and wages and dissolved in summer 2002, the club restarted in the fourth tier as a brand-new entity. Italy international Angelo Di Livio, then 36, refused to flee and joined the phoenix club Associazione Calcio Fiorentina e Florentia Viola. On June 18, 2002, Di Livio was a second-half substitute as Italy were knocked out of the World Cup by South Korea. Three months later, he started for the reformed Fiorentina team as they drew 1-1 at Sangiovannese in the fourth tier of Italian football.

"My other teammates left, but I stayed in [Florence] for a few days to reflect with my family," Di Livio said in an interview with La Nazione. "Then I called [sporting director] Giovanni Galli and said, 'If you want, count on me. I'm staying.'

"I owed it to the Viola fans. In this city there has always been a true, authentic passion. And there was a great desire for rebirth." His 2003 memoir -- part of a great swath of Fiorentina-related literature -- was called "Io resto qui" ("I'm staying here").

"It was a horrible time for Fiorentina fans," Lorenzo Lepore, Fiorentina fan and owner of SV Media, told ESPN. "The club is part of daily life in Florence. It was very hard for Fiorentina fans to accept -- the club hadn't cheated, instead it was the owners who let us down." For Fiorentina, gone were the trips to AC Milan and Inter Milan as they rebuilt, instead they planned for car rides to Aglianese and Poggibonsi.

The scene that greeted players and management on their first days back in as Fiorentia Viola was grim. "I arrived on August 13, but there was nothing," then-manager Pietro Vierchowod said in a 2017 interview. "With sporting director Giovanni Galli, I went to a shop to get balls and shirts, and at the first training sessions I only had five Primavera players. I was the one who recommended [Cristian] Riganò. In the meantime, five or six players arrived at a time, almost all of them not suited to our needs. Once they showed me a videotape of a German who was supposed to come on trial: on the pitch I discovered that it wasn't the one I had seen."

Meanwhile, those who hugged both the glory days and doldrums eras maintained on-field standards. "I told them, 'Guys, we're not here to do a trip, we have to win," Di Livio said. "And I too had to adapt to playing on certain fields."

Rangers players who were there at their lowest ebb know full well the challenges posed by uneven grounds and new surroundings. In February 2012, the Scottish giants were placed into administration over a £9 million unpaid tax bill, and once the full scale of their debts was exposed, the club was voted out of the Scottish Professional Football League. It was taken in by the Scottish Football League and placed in the fourth tier. Some players, such as Steven Naismith and Steven Whittaker, opted not to transfer their contracts to the new holding company responsible for the club and left on free transfers. A few players stayed.

"I'll never forget those first few mornings going to training and seeing the boys disappear one by one," Lee McCulloch said in 2013. "It was heartbreaking -- the strangest experience I've known in my five years at the club.

"I was in contact with most of the boys as we were bouncing things off each other. I know most of them didn't want to leave, but for various reasons they had to move on. I would have preferred the lads to have stayed with Rangers and made the same decision as myself. But I respected and understood where they were coming from. All they were guilty of was looking out for their families and their careers."

On July 29, 2012, Rangers played their first game back in the Ramsdens Cup -- the equivalent of the English Football League Trophy -- at Brechin. After 36 minutes, the match was paused while supporters shook the match ball down from being stuck on a hedge. The club's fans sang "F--- you Celtic, you'll never win this cup." Meanwhile, back in Glasgow, Celtic had their feet up after playing Inter Milan in a preseason friendly the day before.

'We play to feel a sense of belonging'

From the wreck of broken institutions, phoenix clubs can rise (like Panteras Negras FC -- made up of Boavista supporters in Portugal) or teams can regroup and claw their way back up the tree. But the path back to the top is not always straightforward, even for famous institutions.

Rangers won promotion at the end of that season and by 2016-17, they were back in the top flight. But the club has never quite been the same since.

"In the fourth division, it was mad seeing them play in front of 50,000 or so at Ibrox, setting new attendance records," Andy Newport, sportswriter for the Daily Record, told ESPN. "When they got back into the Premiership, there should have been a realization that they had to take things carefully, rather than try and hit a home run off the first ball. They won the league in 2021, but even then [manager] Steven Gerrard was saying postmatch we need to fix the roof while the sun is shining. Every time something goes wrong, there's another reset, another knee-jerk reaction.

"... Since 2012, there's been poor decision-making every turn of the way, slowing down their progress. But under the current American ownership and Derek McInnes, the fans now have proper hope they've figured it out."

French giants Marseille were relegated in 1994 for match-fixing, a year after winning the European Cup. Tony Cascarino, the former Republic of Ireland striker, signed for Marseille after their relegation, charged with getting them back to the French top flight. He remembered walking into the club offices to sign his contract and passing Rudi Voller heading the other way. Voller was leaving the club to sign for Bayer Leverkusen, unwilling to play in Ligue 2. "I feel Marseille have still not recovered from their demotion, and it happened 32 years ago," Cascarino wrote in his column for The Times.

"Before winning the European Cup in 1993, Marseille had won four league titles in a row and had great players such as Chris Waddle, Marcel Desailly and Enzo Francescoli; since then they have won only one, and achieved nothing of note in the Champions League. For them to have won only one French championship this century tells you how damaging that forced relegation in 1993 was."

But out of adversity, heroes emerge. "That season I rediscovered the genuine values ​​of local football," Di Livio said of life in Italy's fourth tier. It was a self-affirming experience for him, as he felt respect from opposition players and managers, while they were fully aware opponents treated matches against his side like they were facing Real Madrid. By 2004, just two years after its dissolution, Di Livio's club had successfully changed its name back to ACF Fiorentina and was back in Serie A.

"What he did was exceptional, like nothing else. The memory of our time relegated will always be there," Lepore says. "We lost players like Adriano, Nuno Gomez and others, and we needed our heroes: like Di Livio and Christian Riganò who scored 30 goals for us that season. He's loved, too."

Even those mired in controversy and disgrace can have their moment of sporting exorcism. When Juventus won the 2012 Serie A title, they partied on the pitch wearing T-shirts with the number 30 written on it -- a tally of trophies including the 2005 and 2006 titles that had been taken away and reallocated. They bathed in their status as chief antagonists.

"The whole Calciopoli thing lent a hand to the Juventus team of that time," Pirlo said. "But to my dying day I'll remain convinced they would have won the same number of trophies relying on their own means, without any kind of external assistance. And that's why I wore a T-shirt with the slogan '30 [titles] won on the pitch' after we clinched the league in Trieste. I came from a world that went to war with Juventus over what happened but, for me, a title that's taken away and then not assigned or handed to another team remains an honor you've won."

Through it all, supporters value loyalty above all else. They remember the badge-kissing and herald those who stay true to the partnership they committed to -- or hold to account those who seek a new admirer. "In football, you can send a message to the outside with loyalty," Buffon told L'Equipe in 2018. "To say to the fans: 'In difficult moments, I'll be there.'

"We play for fame, money, trophies and a lot of things, but we also play to feel a sense of belonging."

stories.headline: Abu Dhabi court reduces sentences for 8 in Nurmagomedov-Dvalishvili brawl
stories.summary: An Abu Dhabi court has reduced the sentences of eight defendants, including six members of Team Nurmagomedov, for their part in last week's wild hotel brawl in the UAE's capital city.
stories.body:
Abu Dhabi's Criminal Court has reduced the sentences of eight defendants convicted in connection to last week's hotel brawl involving Usman Nurmagomedov and Merab Dvalishvili, according to the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department.

The eight defendants, including six members of Team Nurmagomedov, were originally sentenced to six months in prison. Under the revised ruling, which the ADJD released Tuesday, each defendant will instead pay a fine of 150,000 AED (approximately $40,800). The department said the reduced sentence followed a reconciliation between the parties, the mutual withdrawal of claims and appeal by the victim to the Abu Dhabi government for their release.

The altercation took place Nov. 11 in the lobby of the Yas Hilton Hotel, ahead of RAF's inaugural event in Abu Dhabi. Multiple videos captured Nurmagomedov, who is the PFL lightweight champion and younger cousin of Khabib Nurmagomedov, approach Dvalishvili from behind and slap him in the face, triggering a brawl between multiple members of both teams. Dvalishvili, who was initially arrested but released, advocated for Nurmagomedov's release Saturday.

Nurmagomedov and Dvalishvili have been involved in a long-running feud, dating back to Dvalishvili's UFC title win against Umar Nurmagomedov, Usman's older brother, in January 2025. The camps were involved in a brief altercation at another RAF event in July in Dvalishvili's home country of Georgia. Over the weekend, UFC president Dana White criticized RAF's security measures, saying, "They must like it for this to happen all the time."

RAF founder Chad Bronstein told ESPN the organization regretted the incident, but pushed back on any suggestion it's becoming commonplace.

"Did they have drama in the past? Yeah," Bronstein said of Nurmagomedov and Dvalishvili. "But did I think that was going to happen in Abu Dhabi? No. You can always expect there's going to be some words in a press conference ... I didn't think that would happen in a hotel lobby. How many fights have taken place at the UFC, at press conferences, in arenas? We have a great relationship with the UFC, but I think that's an unfair statement."

Bronstein added the incident did not impact RAF's recently-signed deal with the region of Abu Dhabi.

"We're already talking about new events coming up, we have a five-year deal," Bronstein said. "Saturday's event sold out Etihad Arena. I feel like there's going to be a long partnership."

On Monday, RAF announced Dvalishvili and his 21-year-old Georgian teammate Saba Lazishvili have been booked to the promotion's first event in the New York metropolitan area on Dec. 19 at Nassau Coliseum in Long Island.

Dvalishvili will face Kenzo Biyong, a former Dutch professional soccer player from the Netherlands. Lazashvili, who gained a massive online following for his participation in the hotel lobby brawl, will face the winner of a match between Sergio Garcia and Cody Garbrandt at RAF 15 on Nov. 28 in Chicago.

stories.headline: Yankees' Bednar, Twins' Jeffers accept $23.15M qualifying offer
stories.summary: Yankees closer David Bednar and Twins catcher Ryan Jeffers accepted the qualifying offer, returning to their respective teams on a one-year deal worth $23.15M.
stories.body:
New York Yankees closer David Bednar and Minnesota Twins catcher Ryan Jeffers accepted the qualifying offer Tuesday, returning to their respective teams on one-year deals worth $23.15 million.

Five others formally declined the qualifying offer, a list that includes corner outfielders Randy Arozarena (formerly of the Seattle Mariners) and Seiya Suzuki (Chicago Cubs), second baseman Brandon Lowe (Pittsburgh Pirates), reliever Adrian Morejon (San Diego Padres) and starting pitcher Trevor Rogers (Baltimore Orioles).

Former Milwaukee Brewers first baseman Jake Bauers was also extended a qualifying offer but declined in order to sign a four-year, $58 million deal with the Boston Red Sox last week.

The qualifying offer is a one-year deal for the mean salary of Major League Baseball's 125 highest-paid players that is offered to free agents so their prior teams can receive a compensation pick if they sign elsewhere. Players can only be given the qualifying offer once and are only eligible if they spent an entire season on the same team, which is why Tarik Skubal, who was traded from the Detroit Tigers to the Los Angeles Dodgers, wasn't given one.

Bednar, 32, notched 35 saves and put up a 2.47 ERA in 64 games for the Yankees this season, striking out 76 batters and issuing 20 walks in 69⅓ innings. Bednar's 124 saves from 2023 to 2026 are the second most in the majors, trailing only Raisel Iglesias (130). In that time, opponents have slashed just .214/.284/.331 against him.

Jeffers, 29, slashed .256/.353/.461 with 14 home runs and 56 RBIs in 92 games while essentially splitting time with Victor Caratini, who will also return to the Twins. Jeffers' defense graded out as roughly average, but he was among the game's best at controlling counts and put up an OPS above .800 against both lefties and righties. His 8.5 FanGraphs wins above replacement since 2023 is tied for 12th among catchers.

In a normal offseason, Bednar and Jeffers might have hit the open market and sought multiyear deals, but the expiration of the current collective bargaining agreement on Dec. 1 has created a tight window for free agents to sign before owners impose a lockout, freezing transactions. For Bednar and Jeffers, it ultimately made more sense to reenter the market following the 2027 season.

This year's free agent pool, though, is shallow. Arozarena and Suzuki represent the two best outfielders available. Rogers is one of the market's most appealing starters at just 29 years old, and Morejon will undoubtedly get closing opportunities after serving as a dominant setup man in San Diego. Lowe, too, should have plenty of suitors as a left-handed hitter coming off a 4.9-fWAR season at a premium position.

But being tied to the qualifying offer has proven at times to be a hindrance, especially for middle-tier free agents. Competitive balance tax payors must surrender their second- and fifth-highest selections in the upcoming draft, as well as $1 million from their international bonus pools, to sign players tied to a qualifying offer, while revenue-sharing recipients lose their third-highest selection. All other teams forfeit their second-highest draft pick and $500,000 from their international pool in that instance.

Revenue-sharing recipients who lose a player tied to a qualifying offer receive an additional draft pick between the first round and Competitive Balance Round A if the player signs for at least $50 million, while teams who exceed the luxury tax threshold receive the pick after the fourth round.

stories.headline: Nike replaces Adidas as UEFA ball provider to restyle Champions League
stories.summary: The Champions League ball will have a new look next season after Nike replaced Adidas as UEFA's official provider.
stories.body:
The Champions League ball will have a new look next season after Nike replaced Adidas as UEFA's official provider.

A match ball manufactured by Adidas, with the famous star-studded ball used for Europe's premier competition, will be used for the final time in the 2026-27 final.

There has been no confirmation as to whether the new Nike ball will retain the star pattern used in the competitions logo. UEFA said in a statement: "Further details on the match ball designs will be revealed in due course.."

- Why the Champions League's iconic 'star' match ball could soon be replaced

From 2027-28, U.S. brand Nike will take over as the official ball supplier for UEFA for the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League.

German brand Adidas had been the ball supplier for the UEFA Champions League since 2001 but their long-standing association with the competition is now coming to an end.

Nike went into exclusive talks in April with the agency that handles all commercial deals for UEFA club competitions, a subsidiary of United States-based Relevent.

Relevent was appointed last year by the commercial joint venture between UEFA and the increasingly influential European Football Clubs group, which has seen long-standing sponsor deals end.

Relevent was co-founded by Miami Dolphins owner Stephen Ross and also has a long-term deal with UEFA to market commercial rights for national team competitions.

Total broadcast and sponsor revenue for UEFA men's club competitions is projected to rise above 5 billion euros ($5.5 billion) starting next season.

Camilo Andrade, Vice President and General Manager of Nike Football, said: "We are excited and honoured to return to the UEFA Champions League, one of football's biggest stages, after more than two decades, and to bring Nike match balls across UEFA's men's club competitions, including all three major competitions for the first time.

"Football is the world's game, and the ball is at the centre of it, the one thing every player, in every competition, has in common. This is a long-term commitment for Nike. We will listen to the athlete's voice, push the edges of innovation, honour the prestige and tradition of these competitions, and make sure the ball represents the instinct, creativity and joy football brings to billions of fans."

Guy-Laurent Epstein, Co-Managing Director UC3 -- which unites UEFA to Europe's clubs -- said: "We are delighted to welcome Nike as the official match ball provider for UEFA men's club competitions from 2027. Nike brings an incredible combination of sporting heritage, creativity and cultural influence, with an ability to connect with fans around the world. We look forward to working together, both on and off the pitch, to deliver innovation, quality and performance at every level of European club football."

Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Fernando Alonso confirmed for Dakar Rally with Aston Martin
stories.summary: Fernando Alonso will return to the Dakar Rally in January next year as Aston Martin prepares for a surprise debut at the legendary rally raid event.
stories.body:
Fernando Alonso will return to the Dakar Rally in January next year as Aston Martin prepares for a surprise debut at the legendary rally raid event.

The Aston Martin Formula 1 driver, who last took part in the Dakar in 2020 with Toyota, will be joined in a three-car line-up by nine-time world rally champion Sebastien Loeb and world rally raid champion Lucas Moraes.

Working alongside rallying experts Prodrive, Aston Martin has produced a competition-ready rally car that has a tie-in with a military vehicle it developed for use in the video game Call of Duty, Modern Warfare 4. Known as the Dreadnought in both the virtual and real world, the rally car shares very little other than its name with its video-gaming cousin and has been designed specifically to take part in the Dakar Rally, which will return to the continent of Africa next year for the first time since 2007.

Alonso will be joined in his Dreadnought by Marc Coma -- the same co-driver he had in 2020 and a five-time Dakar motorcycle category winner.

"After deciding to continue racing in Formula One with the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team, I thought carefully about Dakar," Alonso, who signed a deal to race with Aston Martin in F1 in September, said.

"In the end, the decision became simple. I wanted to embrace the challenge completely and take on both Formula One and the Dakar Rally in the same year. In 2020, Dakar was one of the most challenging and enjoyable experiences of my career.

"I have enormous respect for this race and the specialists who have mastered it. Having Marc alongside me again is very important, and with Aston Martin, Prodrive, Sébastien and Lucas we have an exceptional team.

"Formula One remains my priority. But I am a racing driver, and challenges like this are why I love competing. I'm looking forward to seeing what we can achieve."

The legendary Dakar Rally was born from a series of rallies that ran from Europe to Africa in the 1970s and held its inaugural event from Paris to Dakar in 1979. Although the route changed through the two continents in the 1990s and early 2000s, the event retained its name before it eventually left Africa in 2008 due to security threats in Mauritania.

Initially the rally found a new home in South America from 2009 to 2019 before moving to Saudi Arabia in 2020, which was the event Alonso took part in and finished 13th driving for Toyota.

In October, it was announced the 2027 event would run from Portugal to Morocco due to security concerns linked to the U.S.-Israel war on Iran and deadly attacks by Yemen's Houthis on Saudi Arabia.

The event will now start in the Algarve and finish in Marrakech, stretching across 12 stages and totaling 4,341km in length. The 2027 Dakar Rally will get underway on January 9 and conclude on January 23.
